project.name: WoGu Sample: Temporal Project
project.description:
Demonstrates wogu-maven-plugin against real Temporal Java SDK code. PaymentWorkflowImpl calls into four service classes under com.example.wogu.sample.services, each grouped by the kind of non-determinism it demonstrates: PaymentService (UUID.randomUUID() for WG001, Thread.sleep() for WG002, System.currentTimeMillis() for WG003), RandomnessService (Math.random() for WG004; new Random()/nextInt() for WG005; ThreadLocalRandom.current() for WG006; new SecureRandom()/nextBytes() for WG007), ConfigurationService (System.getenv() for WG008, System.getProperty() for WG009), and ConcurrencyService (Executors.newFixedThreadPool() for WG010). 'mvn verify' intentionally fails here and writes target/wogu/index.html showing all twelve violations (WG005 and WG007 each report twice: once for the constructor, once for the instance method called on it).
PaymentWorkflowImpl also calls a real Activity (PaymentActivityImpl, via its PaymentActivity interface) whose implementation contains the same UUID/sleep/clock calls; none of those are reported, demonstrating that WoGu's call-graph traversal correctly stops at an Activity implementation's boundary instead of flagging code that isn't subject to workflow replay determinism.
PaymentService.recordAuditId() calls UUID.randomUUID() too, but from inside Workflow.sideEffect(...)'s callback; that call is not reported either, demonstrating that WG001 (like every other rule with suppressedContexts: SIDE_EFFECT) is suppressed inside a Temporal side effect, since Temporal executes it exactly once and replays its recorded result rather than re-running it during replay.
This module is intentionally excluded from the repo's default Maven reactor (see the root pom's 'with-samples' profile), since it fails by design. Run it explicitly: mvn -f sample-temporal-project verify
